title: Normalization of the proper/open comparison under the site comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, and set $\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,T_1,T_2$ be Noetherian schemes (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]), let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] with $u j_1=j_2$. Use constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites and their bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and let
$$e_j:A_Tj^{\mathrm{et}}_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!A_X$$
be the canonical comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], applied termwise to complexes. Let
$$b_u:A_{T_2}Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}A_{T_1}$$
be the canonical derived direct-image comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], with its counit-mate normalization [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Properness makes $u$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, let $\alpha^e_{u,L}:j^{\mathrm{et}}_{2!}L\to Ru_{\mathrm{et},*}j^{\mathrm{et}}_{1!}L$ be the specified map [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], and let $\alpha^p_{u,L}:j^{\mathrm{proet}}_{2!}A_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_{1!}A_XL$ be the canonical proper/open map [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale]. To specify the named map, use the construction in that source: apply exact site-comparison pullback to the specified etale map, and identify the source by the canonical adjoint comparison for open extension by zero and the target by the counit-mate direct-image comparison followed by the open-extension comparison fixed above. Then these named maps satisfy
$$\alpha^p_{u,L}\circ e_{j_2,L}
=Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}(e_{j_1,L})\circ b_{u,j^{\mathrm{et}}_{1!}L}\circ A_{T_2}(\alpha^e_{u,L}).$$
The equality is in $D^+(T_{2,\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, as a map from $A_{T_2}j^{\mathrm{et}}_{2!}L$ to $Ru_{\mathrm{proet},*}j^{\mathrm{proet}}_{1!}A_XL$.

proof.text: Use the positive-level finiteness theorem of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], as already packaged by properOpenNormalizationCoefficientFinite. Expand the named properOpenProEtaleIsoPlus of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale]. Its four factors are the inverse j2 open-extension comparison, the comparison image of the specified etale proper/open arrow, the canonical derived direct-image comparison, and the direct image of the j1 open-extension comparison. The construction already supplies all required invertibility and exact derived functors.

Unfold the abbreviating comparison functor of [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback] and the named direct-image transformation of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. They are definitionally the same functor and transformation appearing in the expanded construction. Apply Iso.trans_hom, Iso.app_hom, Functor.mapIso_hom and asIso_hom to identify its underlying morphism with that four-factor composite. This uses no new geometric comparison or choice of an endpoint isomorphism.

Precompose with the forward j2 open comparison. Iso.hom_inv_id_app_assoc cancels that comparison with its inverse at L. The three remaining factors are exactly the right-hand side of the stated normalization equality.
